sentences.text: Xenotarsosaurus was an abelisaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous.
The known fossils consist of two cotypes: two anterior dorsal vertebrae and a right hind limb containing a 611 mm long femur, tibia, fibula, and ankle bones.
The genus and species Xenotarsosaurus bonapartei were described by Rubén Martínez, Olga Giménez, Jorge Rodríguez, and Graciela Bochatey in 1986.
In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated Xenotarsosaurus to be 6 meters long and weigh 750 kg.
In 2016, the estimated length of Xenotarsosaurus was revised to 5.4 meters.
It has been proposed that Xenotarsosaurus is a neoceratosaurian with uncertain affinities.
Phylogenetic analyses in 2021 placed Xenotarsosaurus as an abelisaurid more derived than Eoabelisaurus.
Xenotarsosaurus lived approximately 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage in what is now South America.
The time range for Xenotarsosaurus is estimated to be between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago.
While originally thought to be from the Campanian stage, the fossils are now believed to date to the earlier Cenomanian–Turonian stages.
